A serious 6-pitch WI5 M7 mixed and ice line up the central weakness of Sloan's west face, established in winter 2025 and finishing with a long steep snow/ice headwall to the summit ridge.

Diamond in the Rough climbs the Southwest Face of Sloan Peak in 9 pitches (~1,100 ft) up to 5.11-, established by Rad Roberts and Brandon Workman on September 11, 2011. It's one of three independent rock lines (with Fire on the Mountain and Northwest Buttress)

Fire on the Mountain climbs 8 pitches of sustained, well-protected alpine rock (to 5.10d) up Sloan's Southwest Face, joining a major ledge that intersects the Corkscrew Route; from there it's roughly 500 ft of 4th-class/low-5th scrambling to the true summit.

face: Left side of the broad west face, exiting onto the north face near the top
overview: A committing 1,800 ft, 9-pitch IV 5.9+ line up the lowest/leftmost corner of Sloan's West Face, first climbed by Mike Preiss and Mark Bunker in 2000. After two funky, thinly-protected opening pitches you're essentially committed to finishing the route and desc

face: Standard route: Sloan Glacier (E/NE) around the S ridge to the Upper West Face
overview: The classic ascent of Sloan Peak's distinctive horn. The route literally spirals around the mountain, crossing the Sloan Glacier and finishing with an exposed Class 3 scramble to the summit. A Mountain Loop landmark visible for miles.

A winter ice line up Sloan's west face established in 2020: an approach pitch of rambly ice into a near-vertical curtain, a long main gully of fat WI3 ice, and a short final step before opening onto the upper snowfields.

New York Gully splits the NW Face of Snoqualmie Mountain, the most-climbed of five parallel ice/mixed lines on that wall (alongside Pineapple Express, Blue Moon, New York Gully Direct, and LA Express). First climbed by Ruch and Cordery-Cotter in 1985 as a IV 5
A short, single-pitch mixed chimney climb just right of the Snot Couloir on Snoqualmie Mountain's northwest face.

face: Southwest Slopes / South Ridge via Cave Ridge
overview: Snoqualmie Mountain is the highest summit rising directly above the Alpental ski area at Snoqualmie Pass, one of the most-climbed scrambles near Seattle for its short approach and big views of Chair Peak, The Tooth, and Guye Peak across the valley. The peak ac
A steep, sustained mixed ice line on Snoqualmie Mountain's northwest face featuring a distinctive ice/snow cave (the route's namesake 'snostril'), finishing near the Thunder Basin exit gully.

breakdown_grades: Glacier travel, short ice steps to ~I2

face: East Ridge / summit tower, southeast side

face: Southwest face, above the Southwest Rib
overview: A well-regarded direct variation to the Southwest Rib, taking a striking double-roof ('money pitch') instead of the standard line before rejoining the Bear Hug pitch.

A free variation eliminating the aid on Mojo Rising, giving a continuously free 5.11- line up this part of the Northwest Face.

A varied alpine free climb up the west face of South Early Winter Spire, beginning low on the northwest face and traversing into the famous double-roof 'Boving Roofs' pitch before finishing up the Southwest Rib. First ascended (aid) by Boving & Pollock in 1976

The Southwest Rib is one of the most popular moderate multipitch alpine rock climbs at Washington Pass, climbing excellent granite on the west face of South Early Winter Spire with a famous dual-offwidth Bear Hug pitch and an airy slabby arete.

The standard, most-climbed route on South Early Winters Spire and the second most popular route in the Liberty Bell Group after the Beckey Route on Liberty Bell — a short, moderate outing well suited to parties wanting the summit with minimal commitment. First

The direct version of South Early Winter Spire's classic East Buttress, climbing harder, steeper pitches low on the buttress before joining the upper line. A sustained, high-quality alpine rock route on excellent Washington Pass granite.

One of the most popular alpine rock routes at Washington Pass — the moderate, classic East Buttress of South Early Winter Spire. Enjoyable, well-featured climbing on excellent granite leads up the buttress to the summit.

Widely regarded as one of the best free rock climbs in the Cascades: a sustained, steep line up the southeast face of South Early Winter Spire on excellent golden granite, with roof pulls and finger cracks low and cleaner crack/corner climbing up high. First a
The original 1937 first-ascent line and the quickest, most moderate route to the summit — a broad snow/ice couloir narrowing toward a fork before a short 5th-class exit move.

Named after the Neil Young song, Southern Man splits off from the Direct East Buttress about halfway up and climbs the south-facing headwall on SEWS's upper south side to the summit. First ascended by Mark Allen, Joel Kauffman, and Leaghan Falley, August 2008

A long, sustained mixed free/bolted line up the steep southeast face of SEWS, starting about 100 ft right of The Passenger. Established over three visits between July and September 2007 by Bryan Burdo and Scott Johnston.

route: Concerto in C for Drill and Hammer
overview: A long, 14-pitch alpine slab climb from a bivy bench up to the summit ridge, featuring sustained 5.8 friction on several pitches and a crusty ridge-running finish above Buckeye Basin.
A 5-pitch, 700-ft route on the Far Western Wall reaching a distinctive hanging flake, with sculpted-knob face climbing low down and a bolt-protected 5.9 face crux on pitch two.

A 12-pitch, 1,500-ft friction climb on immaculate, knobby grey granite, with a polished 5.9 crux on pitch one easing into mostly 5.4-5.6 climbing above, finishing on clean splitter cracks overlooking Whitehorse Mountain.
A 5-pitch, 700-ft moderate slab line up the South Face with two distinct crux pitches sandwiched between easier friction climbing above and below.
A new route on the steep east face of South Peak featuring challenging crack and face climbing on white granite.
